case class Session(token: String, realm: RealmId, user: String)

enum AuthRequest: case SignIn(realm: RealmId, user: String, passwordHash: String, token: String), case SignOut(realm: RealmId, token: String), case SetEnabled(realm: RealmId, user: String, on: Boolean)

    case AuthRequest.SetEnabled(r, u, on) => as.map(a => if a.realm == r && a.username == u then a.copy(enabled = on) else a)

val handleRequest = Node.contract(step)("HandleRequest",
  "A request opens the session a sign-in asks for when the user is enabled, the password theirs and no session holds the token; ends the sessions its sign-out names in its realm; changes accounts only as an administrator's change sets them; and changes nothing else.",
  why = "One request at a time, so each result of the running server is checked; the history's meaning (SignInHistory, Accounts) follows by induction over the requests. Refusing a token an open session holds keeps a token naming one session even if a token were ever drawn twice.",
  idea = "Signing in and out"
)((s, q, t) => t.accounts == administer(s.accounts, q) &&
  t.sessions.forall(x => (s.sessions.contains(x) && !endedBy(q, x)) || opened(s, q) == Some(x)) &&
  s.sessions.forall(x => endedBy(q, x) || t.sessions.contains(x)) &&
  opened(s, q).forall(x => t.sessions.contains(x)))
  .under(sessionsMirrorSignIns, accountsAsAdministered)

    expect(ServerState(loaded, List(Session("t1", acme, "alice"))), AuthRequest.SignOut(acme, "t1"), ServerState(loaded, Nil),

back its token, a value no other session has. Anyone else gets no session.

A user can sign out with their token: its session ends at once.

val introspectContract = referenceTokens.contractVia[RealmId, String, Option[Claims]](
  "Introspect",
  "An introspection answers with the token's user and their roles exactly when the token's session is open in the realm asking and the user is enabled there; the claims name that realm.",
  why = "ReferenceTokens for one request, as Keycloak's introspection endpoint answers it: the claims carry the user's realm roles, which applications use to authorise. abs: the user an answer names."
)(abs = f => (r, t) => claimedUser(f(r, t)))((realm, token, res) =>
  res.forall(c => c.realm == realm && sessionsByToken(token).exists(s => s.realm == realm && s.user == c.user) &&
    users.value.exists(a => a.realm == realm && a.username == c.user && a.enabled && a.roles == c.roles)) &&
  sessionsByToken(token).forall(s => (s.realm == realm && isEnabled(realm, s.user)) ==> res.isDefined))
  .examples(
    users.bind(List(UserAccount(RealmId("acme"), "alice", "h-alice", true, List("admin", "user")), UserAccount(RealmId("acme"), "bob", "h-bob", false, List("user")))),
    sessionsByToken.bindTable(Map("t1" -> Session("t1", RealmId("acme"), "alice"), "t2" -> Session("t2", RealmId("acme"), "bob"))),
    sessionDb.bind(SessionDb.of(List(Session("t1", RealmId("acme"), "alice"), Session("t2", RealmId("acme"), "bob")))))(
    expect(RealmId("acme"), "t1", Some(Claims(RealmId("acme"), "alice", List("admin", "user"))), "Alice's token at acme: active, with her roles"),
    expect(RealmId("globex"), "t1", None, "acme's token is not good at globex"),
    expect(RealmId("acme"), "t2", None, "Bob was disabled after signing in: his token is no longer active"),
    expect(RealmId("acme"), "t9", None, "no session: signed out, or never issued"),
    reject(RealmId("globex"), "t1", Some(Claims(RealmId("globex"), "alice", List("admin", "user"))), "a token is never good in another realm"),
    reject(RealmId("acme"), "t2", Some(Claims(RealmId("acme"), "bob", List("user"))), "a disabled user's token is never active"),
    reject(RealmId("acme"), "t1", Some(Claims(RealmId("acme"), "alice", List("admin", "user", "owner"))), "roles are never made up"),
    reject(RealmId("acme"), "t1", None, "an active token is not turned away"))
  .keeps(realmIsolation)((realm, token, res) => res match
    case Some(c) => List((realm, c))
    case None    => Nil)
  .expects("A token with no stored session is never active, in any realm")(f =>
    forall((r: RealmId, t: String) => (sessionsByToken(t) == None) ==> (f(r, t) == None)))

content.idea:
# Realms: a small authentication server

Several organisations share one authentication server, like Keycloak. Each
organisation is a realm with its own users. Applications never see passwords:
they send users to the server to sign in, and ask the server whose a token is.

## Signing in and out

A user of a realm can sign in with their username and password. If the user
is enabled and the password is theirs, the server opens a session and gives
back its token, a value no other session has. Anyone else gets no session.

A user can sign out with their token: its session ends at once.

- Token expiry and refresh tokens.
- Which applications may ask (client authentication), consent, and the
  OpenID Connect discovery documents.
- Managing realms and users: they are loaded at start, and an administrator
  can enable or disable a user.

    case AuthRequest.SignIn(_, _, _, _)   => as
    case AuthRequest.SignOut(_, _)        => as

# Realms: a small authentication server

Several organisations share one authentication server, like Keycloak. Each
organisation is a realm with its own users. Applications never see passwords:
they send users to the server to sign in, and ask the server whose a token is.

An application of a realm can ask the server whose a token is. The server
answers with the user and their roles in that realm exactly when the token's
session is open in that realm and the user is still enabled; otherwise the
token is not active.

A token is only ever good in the realm that issued it.
